============================================================================= Function Block : AutoStarter
Purpose: Automatically cycles a start command until the equipment reports that it is running or the engagement request is removed.
Application: Use to control equipment that requires an engagement delay followed by repeated timed start attempts.
Operation: 1. When xEngage is TRUE, wait for tEngaging. 2. Assert xStart for tStarting, then wait for tEngaging before the next start attempt. 3. Stop the cycle when xRunning is TRUE or xEngage is FALSE.
Inputs: tEngaging - Delay between start attempts (default T#3S). tStarting - Duration of each start command (default T#3S). xRunning - Running feedback; ends the start cycle when TRUE. xEngage - Start-cycle request; the cycle ends when FALSE.
Outputs: xStart - Timed start command, asserted during each start attempt.
InOut: None.
Alarms/Faults: None. There is no dedicated fault or timeout output.
Assumptions: - Call the function block cyclically. - xRunning is driven by valid equipment running feedback. - Keep xEngage TRUE while start attempts are required.
Limitations: - The block does not detect or report a failed start; it continues cycling until running feedback is received or xEngage is removed. - Timing resolution depends on the PLC task cycle.
Dependencies: - None.
Example:
fbAutoStarter( tEngaging := T#3S, tStarting := T#3S, xRunning := xMotorRunning, xEngage := xAutoStart ); xMotorStart := fbAutoStarter.xStart;

================================================================================ Function : AU8_TO_U16
Purpose: Combines two USINT values from an array into a UINT, with the byte at i32Lo as the low byte and the byte at i32Hi as the high byte.
Application: Decode a 16-bit little-endian value stored in two bytes of a USINT array. This function is not little- or big-endian oriented: the low byte is supplied at i32Lo and the high byte at i32Hi, regardless of their array index order.
Inputs: i32Lo - Array index of the low byte. i32Hi - Array index of the high byte. u16XX - UINT fallback returned when either index is outside the array. au8 - Source array of USINT values.
Return Value: UINT - The combined 16-bit value, or u16XX if either index is outside the array bounds.
Assumptions: - The array contains the bytes to decode at the specified indices. - The byte at i32Lo is the least significant byte; the byte at i32Hi is the most significant byte. - For example, bytes 16#34 at i32Lo and 16#12 at i32Hi produce 16#1234.
Limitations: - Invalid indices are indicated only by returning u16XX; there is no separate error status, so this value may be indistinguishable from a valid result. - The function does not require the indices to be adjacent or ordered. - Big-endian data must be mapped so i32Hi selects the high byte and i32Lo selects the low byte. Typically, big-endian data is stored with the high byte first in the array. Hence, for big-endian data, i32Hi should be the index of the first byte and i32Lo should be the index of the second byte.
Example:
uiValue := AU8_TO_U16( i32Lo := 0, i32Hi := 1, u16XX := UINT#0, au8 := au8Data );
